concepts.title: Degree of a Polynomial
concepts.definition: The degree of a polynomial is the highest power of the variable with a non-zero coefficient.
concepts.formula: degree(p(x)) = max exponent of x with non-zero coefficient
concepts.key_idea: A polynomial of degree n has at most n zeros and the leading term determines the degree.
question_patterns: find the degree of the given polynomial
identify whether the expression is a polynomial and find its degree
classify polynomial as linear quadratic or cubic based on degree
determine degree of a polynomial in standard form
find degree of a polynomial given its terms

solution_steps.action: Write each term as coefficient times a power of x
solution_steps.explain: Standard form makes every exponent visible.
Terms with zero coefficient do not count towards the degree.
Degree 1 is linear, 2 is quadratic, 3 is cubic; higher degrees stay unnamed.

worked_examples.question: Find the degree of the polynomial 3x^4 - 5x^2 + 7x - 9.
worked_examples.solution: The highest power of x with non-zero coefficient is 4.

worked_examples.question: Identify the degree of x^2 - 3x + 2 and classify it.
worked_examples.solution: Highest exponent is 2, so it is a quadratic polynomial.

exercises.question: Find the degree of the polynomial 5x^3 - 2x^2 + x - 7.
Classify the polynomial 7 - 4x + x^2 by its degree.

concepts.title: Zeros of a Polynomial
concepts.definition: A zero of a polynomial p(x) is a real number k such that p(k) = 0. Zeros are also called roots of the polynomial.
concepts.formula: p(k) = 0 implies k is a zero of p(x)
concepts.key_idea: A polynomial of degree n has at most n real zeros; zeros are the x-intercepts of the graph y = p(x).
question_patterns: check whether a given value is a zero of the polynomial
find all zeros of the given polynomial
verify that a number is a zero of the polynomial
determine number of zeros of a polynomial
find zeros of a linear polynomial

solution_steps.action: Substitute the candidate value k into the polynomial
solution_steps.explain: Replace x with k everywhere in p(x).
Work out the arithmetic to a single number.
If the value is 0 then k is a zero of the polynomial; otherwise it is not.

worked_examples.question: Check whether 2 is a zero of p(x) = x^2 - 3x + 2.

exercises.question: Verify whether -1 is a zero of p(x) = x^2 + 2x + 1.
Find the zero of the polynomial p(x) = 5x + 10.

concepts.title: Relationship Between Zeros and Coefficients of Quadratic Polynomials
concepts.definition: For a quadratic polynomial ax^2 + bx + c with zeros alpha and beta, the sum of zeros = -b/a and the product of zeros = c/a.
concepts.key_idea: The zeros of a quadratic polynomial are directly related to the ratios of its coefficients.
question_patterns: find sum and product of zeros of quadratic polynomial
verify relationship between zeros and coefficients
find a quadratic polynomial given sum and product of zeros
check if given zeros satisfy coefficient relationship
find coefficients given zeros of quadratic polynomial

solution_steps.explain: Write the polynomial in standard form ax^2 + bx + c.

solution_steps.action: Compute sum and product of zeros
solution_steps.explain: Calculate alpha + beta and alpha * beta from the given zeros.
Check that sum equals -b/a and product equals c/a.

worked_examples.question: Find the sum and product of zeros of p(x) = x^2 - 7x + 10.
Verify that 2 and 5 are zeros of x^2 - 7x + 10 and check the coefficient relationship.

exercises.question: Find the sum and product of zeros of 2x^2 - 8x + 6.
Verify the relationship between zeros and coefficients for x^2 + 5x + 6 with zeros -2 and -3.

concepts.title: Finding Zeros by Quadratic Formula
concepts.definition: The zeros of a quadratic polynomial ax^2 + bx + c are given by the quadratic formula x = (-b +- sqrt(b^2 - 4ac)) / 2a.
concepts.key_idea: The discriminant D = b^2 - 4ac determines whether zeros are real and distinct, equal, or not real.
question_patterns: find zeros of quadratic polynomial using quadratic formula
compute roots using the quadratic formula
find zeros when factorization is not possible
use quadratic formula to solve polynomial equation
find roots given coefficients a b c

solution_steps.explain: D = b^2 - 4ac decides whether real zeroes exist.

solution_steps.action: Take the square root of D
solution_steps.explain: Needed only when D is non-negative.
Substitute into x = (-b +- sqrt(D)) / 2a to obtain both zeroes.

worked_examples.question: Find the zeros of 2x^2 - 7x + 3 using the quadratic formula.
Find the zeros of x^2 - 4x + 1 using the quadratic formula.

exercises.question: Find the zeros of 3x^2 - 5x + 1 using the quadratic formula.
Find the zeros of x^2 - 6x + 4 using the quadratic formula.

concepts.title: Constructing a Polynomial from Given Zeros
concepts.definition: A quadratic polynomial with zeros alpha and beta can be written as k(x^2 - (alpha+beta)x + alpha*beta) for any non-zero constant k.
concepts.formula: p(x) = k(x - alpha)(x - beta) = k(x^2 - (alpha+beta)x + alpha*beta)
concepts.key_idea: Use the sum and product of given zeros to construct the polynomial; k is any non-zero scalar.
question_patterns: find a quadratic polynomial with given zeros
construct polynomial given sum and product of zeros
form a quadratic polynomial whose zeros are given
find polynomial with given sum and product of zeros
write a quadratic polynomial from its roots

solution_steps.action: Compute the sum and product of the given zeroes
solution_steps.explain: Add the zeroes and multiply them.
Write x^2 - (sum)x + (product), optionally times a non-zero constant k.
Collect the terms to read off a, b and c.

worked_examples.question: Find a quadratic polynomial whose sum and product of zeros are 4 and 1 respectively.
Find a quadratic polynomial whose zeros are 2 and -3.

exercises.question: Find a quadratic polynomial whose sum and product of zeros are -1 and -20 respectively.

concepts.title: Division Algorithm for Polynomials
concepts.definition: If p(x) and g(x) are any two polynomials with g(x) != 0, then p(x) = g(x)*q(x) + r(x) where degree of r(x) < degree of g(x) or r(x) = 0.
concepts.key_idea: Polynomial division is analogous to integer division; the remainder has degree less than the divisor.
question_patterns: divide one polynomial by another and find quotient and remainder
apply division algorithm to find quotient and remainder
find remainder when polynomial is divided by another
verify division algorithm for given polynomials
find quotient using long division of polynomials

solution_steps.explain: Leading term of dividend divided by leading term of divisor gives the next quotient term.
Multiply the divisor by that quotient term and subtract from the working dividend.
Continue until the remainder has degree lower than the divisor; the collected terms form the quotient.

worked_examples.question: Divide p(x) = x^3 - 3x^2 + 5x - 3 by g(x) = x - 1 and find quotient and remainder.
worked_examples.solution: Long division gives quotient x^2 - 2x + 3 and remainder 0.

exercises.question: Divide x^3 + 3x^2 + 3x + 1 by x + 1 and find quotient and remainder.
Verify the division algorithm for p(x) = x^3 - 6x^2 + 11x - 6 and g(x) = x - 2.

concepts.title: Factor Theorem
concepts.definition: For a polynomial p(x), (x - a) is a factor of p(x) if and only if p(a) = 0.
concepts.formula: (x - a) is a factor of p(x) iff p(a) = 0
concepts.key_idea: The factor theorem connects the zeros of a polynomial with its linear factors; it is a special case of the remainder theorem.
question_patterns: check whether x - a is a factor of the polynomial
use factor theorem to determine if a is a zero
verify factor theorem for given polynomial
find a factor of the polynomial using factor theorem
determine if x + a is a factor using factor theorem

solution_steps.explain: Extract the value a from the proposed linear factor.
Substitute x = a into the polynomial and compute the value.
If p(a) = 0 then (x - a) is a factor; otherwise it is not.

worked_examples.question: Check whether x - 2 is a factor of p(x) = x^3 - 3x^2 + 4x - 4.
Determine whether x + 1 is a factor of x^3 + x^2 + x + 1.

exercises.question: Check whether x - 3 is a factor of x^3 - 6x^2 + 11x - 6.

concepts.title: Graphical Representation of Polynomial Zeros
concepts.definition: The zeros of a polynomial p(x) are the x-coordinates of the points where the graph y = p(x) intersects the x-axis.
concepts.formula: Zeros of p(x) = x-intercepts of graph y = p(x)
concepts.key_idea: A polynomial of degree n intersects the x-axis at most n times; the number of x-intercepts equals the number of real zeros.
question_patterns: find number of zeros from the graph of polynomial
determine zeros from x-intercepts of graph
sketch graph of polynomial and find zeros
identify number of real zeros from graph
relate graph of polynomial to its zeros

solution_steps.explain: Plot y = p(x) on the coordinate plane.
The zeroes are exactly the x-coordinates where the graph meets the x-axis.
The number of cutting points bounds the number of zeroes of the polynomial.

worked_examples.question: The graph of y = x^2 - 4 intersects the x-axis at x = 2 and x = -2. Find the zeros.
worked_examples.solution: The x-intercepts are at x = 2 and x = -2, so the zeros are 2 and -2.

worked_examples.question: A quadratic polynomial graph does not intersect the x-axis. How many real zeros does it have?
worked_examples.solution: No x-intercepts means no real zeros.

exercises.question: The graph of y = x^2 - 5x + 6 intersects the x-axis at x = 2 and x = 3. Find the zeros.
A cubic polynomial graph intersects the x-axis at 3 points. How many real zeros does it have?
